section.book: Bittinger, Beecher, Ellenbogen & Penna, College Algebra: Graphs and Models, 7e
section.title: Analyzing Graphs of Quadratic Functions

title: Write f(x) in vertex form by completing the square; read the vertex
sources: OpenStax College Algebra 2e §5.1 pp. 395-399 (CC BY 4.0): explanations only, no problems copied
process_card: Writing f(x) in vertex form by completing the square

problem.prompt: Write f(x) = {tex:f} in the form a(x - h)^2 + k and find the vertex.

steps.name: factor a out of the x-terms
add the square of half the x-coefficient (subtract it too)
move the subtracted number outside (times a)
write the perfect square as a squared binomial

mistakes.name: read h with the wrong sign
mistakes.message: (x + 5)^2 is (x - (-5))^2, so h = -5: the sign flips.

mistakes.name: moved the subtracted number out without multiplying by a
mistakes.message: The number you subtracted was inside a( ... ): it comes out multiplied by a.

hints.step: factor a out of the x-terms
hints.hint: Write a( x^2 + (b/a)x ) and leave c outside.
hints.why: Completing the square needs x^2 with coefficient 1.

hints.step: add the square of half the x-coefficient (subtract it too)
hints.hint: Half of the x-coefficient, squared: add it and subtract it inside.
hints.why: Adding 0 in total leaves f(x) unchanged.

hints.step: move the subtracted number outside (times a)
hints.hint: Take the minus term out of the parentheses and multiply it by a.
hints.why: a multiplies everything inside the parentheses.

hints.step: write the perfect square as a squared binomial
hints.why: That is the vertex form a(x - h)^2 + k.

hints.hint: h has the opposite sign of the number in the parentheses.
hints.why: In a(x - h)^2 + k the vertex is (h, k).
